assays.assay_description: Mice injected i.p. with saline or psilocybin (0.3, 2, 10 mg/kg) and immediately placed in a transparent acrylic arena (68 x 22 x 26 cm); trained observer recorded head twitches and rearing bouts in 2-minute intervals over 20 minutes.

application_type.evidence: treated with 0.3, 2, or 10 mg/kg of psilocybin or saline (i.p.)

setup_habituation.evidence: Only room acclimation described: 'animals were acclimatized for at least 90 minutes in a dimly lit room'; no apparatus pre-exposure reported.

setup_restrain.evidence: immediately placed in a transparent acrylic arena (68 × 22 x 26 cm) for observation over 20 minutes

food_restriction.evidence: No food described in the acrylic observation arena.

water_restriction.evidence: No water described in the acrylic observation arena.

time_to_assay.evidence: treated with ... psilocybin or saline (i.p.), and immediately placed in a transparent acrylic arena

sample_size.evidence: saline N =10 [7 M/3 F]; 0.3 mg/kg N =6 [3 M/3 F]; 2 mg/kg N =10 [7 M/3 F]; 10 mg/kg N =6 [3 M/3 F]

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin dose-dependently increased head twitch responses and dose-dependently decreased rearing bouts, confirming physiological activity across 0.3-10 mg/kg. Effects seen in both sexes but the study was not powered to detect sex differences.
outcomes.statistics: HTR: One-way ANOVA F(3,28) = 42.98, P < 0.000001, Tukey *P<0.05 vs saline; Rearing: F(3,28) = 15.96, P = 0.000003, Tukey *P<0.05 vs saline
outcomes.evidence: We confirmed that psilocybin was physiologically active over the dose range (0.3, 2, and 10 mg/kg) by observing a dose-dependent increase in head twitch response (HTR) ... and a decrease in rearing behaviors

B1_num_measures.evidence: A trained observer (A.B.C.) recorded head twitch responses and rearing behaviors

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: recorded head twitch responses and rearing behaviors in 2-minute intervals

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No transition or bout-structure analysis reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Rearing bouts were defined by an unsupported or supported upward movement of the rostral portion of the animal with its forepaws raised off the ground

B7_automated_classification.evidence: A trained observer (A.B.C.) recorded head twitch responses and rearing behaviors

E2_shelter.evidence: No shelter described in the arena.

E3_bedding.evidence: No bedding described in the acrylic arena.

E7_social_context.evidence: each animal placed in arena individually and returned to its home cage after testing

E8_food_water.evidence: No food/water described in the arena.

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug recording; animals placed in arena immediately after injection.

assays.assay_description: Calibrated von Frey filaments applied to lateral plantar hind paw (up-down design) in plexiglass enclosures on a perforated metal floor; paw withdrawal threshold measured in naive, CFA, SNI, AIMP (cutaneous) mice at pre-drug and 1, 4, 24 h after psilocybin in acute and chronic pain phases; morphine comparator in CFA.

application_type.evidence: Mice were dosed intraperitoneally at 0.3, 2, or 10 mg/kg (psilocybin)

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice were acclimated to the testing chamber for 1 -2days prior to the start of the study (1 h/session).

setup_restrain.evidence: placing mice in plexiglass enclosures mounted onto a testing platform with a metal, perforated floor

food_restriction.evidence: No food described in the testing enclosures.

water_restriction.evidence: No water described in the testing enclosures.

time_to_assay.evidence: a 3-point dose-response curve at multiple time points (1, 4, and 24 hours after drug injection) during both acute and chronic pain phases

sample_size.evidence: Fig 1C: N =5/group, all M; SNI (N =12 [6 M/6 F] per group); AIMP (CON N =14; AIMP+PSI 10 mg/kg N =10 [5 M/5 F]); CFA (N =8 [4 M/4 F] per group)

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin (0.3, 2, 10 mg/kg) did not alter mechanical sensitivity in naive mice or mechanical hypersensitivity in SNI, AIMP or CFA models at 1, 4 or 24 h in either acute or chronic phase, whereas morphine reversed CFA mechanical hyperalgesia. No sex differences.
outcomes.statistics: Fig1C: F(2.904, 23.2) = 103.0, P<0.000001; SNI: dose F[4,450] = 553.42, time F[8,450] = 121.31, sex F[1,450] = 0.00, P=0.960, dose×time F[32,450] = 8.87; AIMP cutaneous (Fig S2E); CFA: dose F[4,270] = 274.38, time F[8,270] = 66.33, dose×time F[32,270] = 4.25 (effects driven by pain model vs CON)
outcomes.evidence: None of the psilocybin doses administered altered the established thermal or mechanical hypersensitivity at any of the acute time points tested. Two weeks later, a second dose of psilocybin was given, and again, no effect on thermal or mechanical hypersensitivity was observed.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Manual filament application and response scoring.

E1_environment_type.evidence: plexiglass enclosures mounted onto a testing platform with a metal, perforated floor

D1_continuity.evidence: multiple time points (1, 4, and 24 hours after drug injection) during both acute and chronic pain phases

D2_session_duration.evidence: not reported (testing duration not stated; 1 h acclimation is not recording)

D3_recording_days.evidence: Testing at acute phase (injection day + 24 h) and chronic phase two weeks later (injection day + 24 h), plus baseline

D4_baseline.evidence: Post-hoc Bonferroni test, *P <0.05 across pre-MOR vs 30 m post-MOR for mechanical and thermal tests; Fig 2 includes pre-drug time points

assays.assay_description: Radiant heat applied to plantar hind paw in plexiglass enclosures on a glass platform; withdrawal latency (30 s cutoff, 2-3 trials averaged) measured in CFA, SNI, AIMP mice at pre-drug and 1, 4, 24 h after psilocybin in acute and chronic phases; morphine comparator.

setup_habituation.evidence: The animals were acclimatized to the testing environment for 1 -2dayspriorto the start of the study (1 h/session).

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin did not alter thermal (heat) hypersensitivity in SNI, AIMP or CFA models at any dose or time point, whereas morphine was antinociceptive. The only exception was a reduction in thermal sensitivity in females at 0.3 mg/kg, 4 h post-injection in the chronic AIMP phase.
outcomes.evidence: We did observe a reduction in thermal sensitivity at a single dose and time point in females (0.3 mg/kg, 4 hours after psilocybin injection at the chronic time point, Fig S1K), otherwise psilocybin had no effect on thermal sensitivity.

setup_restrain.evidence: One mouse was then placed into each cage and left undisturbed for fifteen minutes.

food_restriction.evidence: No food on the temperature plates.

water_restriction.evidence: No water on the temperature plates.

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin dose-dependently produced preference for the 40 °C plate in CFA and naive mice and dose-dependent avoidance of the 20 °C plate, interpreted as warmth-seeking secondary to hypothermia rather than analgesia; morphine blocked CFA-induced heat avoidance. outcomes.summary: Acute psilocybin dose-dependently decreased formalin-induced cold sensitivity, but had no effect on cold sensitivity in SNI at any time point in acute or chronic phases; the formalin effect was attributed to psilocybin-induced hypothermia.

judge_notes: Retained 8 behavioural assays agreed by all candidates (HTR+rearing as a single observational session; von Frey; Hargreaves; muscle withdrawal threshold; marble burying; mouse grimace scale; thermal place preference; cold plate). Thermal-camera body temperature excluded as a purely physiological measure.

HTR/rearing: B1 set to 1 (2 measures; gemma's score 2 inconsistent with 2-3 category); B2=Yes (2-min interval recording, 2/3 candidates); B4=Yes (rearing is natural exploratory act scored as discrete bouts, 2/3 candidates); setup_habituation overridden to not_reported because only room acclimation is described.

Von Frey/Hargreaves/MWT: D2 scored 0 with low confidence because session duration is not stated; D3 = 2-7 days (modal); D4 set to Yes (medium) because Fig 1C/D report pre-MOR vs post-drug values and Fig 2 analysis includes pre-drug time points (9 time points); D5 = Yes for 24 h post-dose testing.

Marble burying: E1 kept as Standard apparatus (empty standard habitat, not the animal's own home cage); 24-h re-test (Fig S1F) counted as a second session/day (D1=Multiple, D3=2-7); D2=15 min -> 1 (gemma's 0 was a boundary error).

Thermal place preference: B1 = 1 measure (preference/zone time); B7 = Yes per rubric (SLEAP pose estimation + SimBA); sex_dependent set to 'yes' (medium) based on 'This effect appears stronger in female mice at the 2 mg/kg and 10 mg/kg doses'.
Dosing schedule set to 'repeated' because pain-model animals received a second psilocybin dose two weeks later; morphine and buprenorphine comparators added as separate dosing entries.
Mouse grimace setup_restrain = no (plastic enclosure, freely moving; 2/3 candidates). Cold plate direction = decrease (reduced formalin-induced cold sensitivity; null in SNI).
